A COMMON HIRING MISTAKE

before: A revenue target does not prove you need another salesperson.
after: A revenue gap doesn’t mean you need another salesperson.

before: A company can be short of revenue and still have enough selling capacity. The real constraint may be pipeline, conversion, territory supply, founder dependence, ramp timing or management capacity.
after: A company can be short of revenue and still have enough sellers. The real limit may be too little pipeline, a low win rate, too few accounts to sell into, deals that only close when the founder sells them, the time a new hire needs to ramp, or no one with time to manage them.

before: The analysis separates the revenue problem from the headcount question.
after: The analysis looks at the revenue gap and the hiring question separately, so you can see which problem you actually have.
WHAT WE CHECK

before: Four things have to survive the math.
after: Another AE is supported only if four things hold up in the numbers.
01 — Revenue need

before: We compare the revenue plan with the productive capacity already in the system.
after: We compare your revenue plan with what your current sellers can realistically close.
02 — Pipeline

before: Is there enough qualified opportunity for another seat?
after: Is there enough qualified pipeline for another seller?

before: We test whether allocatable pipeline and pipeline creation can feed the proposed seller.
after: We check whether there is enough existing pipeline to hand the new seller, and whether you create new opportunities fast enough to keep them busy.

before: Can another seller reproduce the motion?
after: Can someone other than the founder close these deals?

before: We separate founder-led success from evidence that a non-founder seller can run the motion.
after: We separate the deals the founder closed from the deals other sellers closed, and check whether there are enough of the second kind to plan on.

before: We reconcile recruiting timing, ramp, sales cycle and management capacity.
after: We add up the time it takes to recruit, ramp and close a first deal, and check that someone has time to manage the new hire.
THE MATH

before: Start with the revenue. Work backward until the seat either holds or breaks.
after: We start with the revenue you need and work backward to the pipeline one more seller would require.

before: That is only the beginning. We then ask whether the existing team already has unused capacity, whether the pipeline can actually be allocated to the new seller, whether the conversion rate is transferable beyond the founder, and whether the revenue can arrive inside the required period.
after: That is only the first step. We then check whether your current team has room for more deals, whether that pipeline can actually be handed to a new seller, whether your win rate holds up when the founder isn’t selling, and whether the revenue can close within the period your plan needs it.

before: The question is not whether you want another AE. It is whether the system can supply what that AE would need to produce.
after: The question isn’t whether you want another AE. It’s whether your business can give that AE the pipeline and support they would need to reach their quota.

YES, WITH CONDITIONS
Main limit: not enough qualified pipeline

before: Another AE can be economically justified by the revenue plan, but the current pipeline-production rate does not yet support three fully productive sellers.
after: The revenue plan justifies a third AE, but the business doesn’t yet create enough qualified pipeline to keep three sellers fully busy.

before: At the declared conversion rate, the proposed seat requires more qualified opportunity supply than is currently allocatable after the existing team’s demand is accounted for.
after: At a 21% win rate, the new seller would need more qualified opportunities than are left over once the two current AEs have theirs.
The hire is supported once:

before: allocatable qualified pipeline reaches the required coverage for the proposed contribution period;
after: the qualified pipeline the new AE can take over is large enough to cover what they are expected to close in the plan period;

before: monthly qualified opportunity creation supports the additional seller after existing-team demand;
after: the business creates enough new qualified opportunities each month to feed a third seller as well as the current two;

before: non-founder conversion evidence is strong enough to use as the planning rate;
after: the win rate on deals the founder didn’t sell is known well enough to plan on;

before: the start date still allows the seller to contribute inside the required revenue window.
after: the start date still leaves time for the new seller to close revenue inside the plan period.
